claims.text: A small, calm garden café with a relaxed atmosphere where a simple order of black coffee or plain tea is straightforward.
Core dishes (omurice, breaded pork cutlet, curry) are flour- and wheat-based and prepared in a shared kissaten kitchen; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Signature items rely on egg, butter, and meat, with no vegan options noted; vegan diners cannot be reliably accommodated.
The signature plate is centered on shrimp, keema (minced meat), and chicken curries served on a shared plate, with only the dal potentially plant-based and no documented vegan preparation.

name: 轉害坊（転害坊） (Tengaibou (Cafe Gallery Tengaibou))

claims.text: Coffee is roasted in-house from green beans daily and served fresh, so the core drink is a simple single-ingredient preparation.

name: THE BURGER STAND MAVERICK（マーベリック） (The Burger Stand Maverick)

claims.text: The Teriyaki Burger uses a Japanese soy-based sauce, which typically contains wheat.

name: 東大寺絵馬堂茶屋 (Todaiji Emado Chaya)

claims.text: Wheat noodles (udon, soba, nyumen/somen) are central to the menu and share a kitchen, so cross-contact for celiacs is likely; no gluten-free protocol is documented.
Pickles and tsukudani accompaniments served with the chagayu are typically seasoned with standard (wheat-based) soy sauce; no wheat-free soy sauce is indicated.
Noodle dishes use fish/bonito dashi and one menu item is herring soba, so animal products are present in the kitchen; vegan diners would need to confirm broth and seasoning for any dish.
The chagayu is plain hojicha-roasted rice porridge, naturally free of wheat in the porridge itself, and comes with vegetable pickles that can be chosen to taste.

name: 東大寺二月堂南茶所　龍美堂 (Todaiji Nigatsudo Minami Chajo Ryubido)

claims.text: Signature warabi mochi is made from bracken starch and kinako rather than wheat flour, and ohagi is glutinous rice with red-bean paste — base recipes that typically contain no wheat and no animal products.

name: とおく＆らいぶcafé 葉音（ぱおん） (Tooku & Live cafe Paon)

claims.text: Focus on fair-trade coffee and natural/organic light foods suggests an ingredient-conscious kitchen, though no specific allergen handling is documented.
